extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, patent stakeholders (companies, universities, inventors), patent attorneys, and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the provisions of H.R. 1908 (Patent Reform Act of 2007) that aim to change U.S. patent examination, issuance, and litigation rules to improve patent quality, reduce abusive litigation, and align U.S. law with international practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file patent system
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill implements a first-to-file patent system, which is in line with other countries and will streamline the patent review and issuance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning U.S. practice with international first-to-file norms is presented as a way to streamline review and issuance; intended to reduce uncertainties tied to priority disputes under first-to-invent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant opposition / strengthened inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision significantly strengthens the post-grant interparty’s reexamination process and creates a post-grant opposition procedure to allow the private sector to challenge a patent just after it is approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure that parties contesting validity have a full and complete opportunity to make their case within the Patent Office before final issuance; described as an effective, less costly alternative to court litigation and a means to improve patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission of prior art during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrects the flaw that the existing patent process contains no avenue for third parties who may possess information about prior art to submit that to the patent examiner while the application is being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing third parties to submit prior art during examination is framed as enabling examiners to access important information, thereby improving patent quality by preventing issuance of patents on non-novel or previously used inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of patent applications before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement (from prior reform) that patents be published before they’re granted; publication is discussed as a tool to improve patent quality and examiner searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication before grant increases the visibility of pending applications and prior art, aiding examiners and third parties in identifying potentially relevant prior art and improving overall examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for willful infringement and notice specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill deals with willful infringement and creates clearer standards by requiring greater specificity in notice letters alleging infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring specific notice letters and clearer willfulness standards is intended to reduce opportunistic claims of willfulness and provide fairer bases for enhanced damages; also tied to requiring courts to include in the record information about how they calculate damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages proportionality and limits on excessive awards
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 1908 prohibits excessive damage awards and contains provisions to help ensure that damages are proportional to the value the patent added to the overall product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting damages to the value added by the patented invention injects certainty into awards, reduces the potential windfalls from litigation, and is presented as fostering investment in R&D rather than defensive litigation spending; courts may be required to document calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue reform to prevent forum shopping
rubrics_metrics.description: Tightens venue provisions in patent law to prevent forum shopping; cases would be allowed where the defendant is located or has committed acts relevant to the patent dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to combat concentration of plaintiff-friendly filings (e.g., Eastern District of Texas), reduce artificially favorable venues for ‘patent trolls,’ and restore fairness; special, freer rules retained for independent inventors and universities while corporate plaintiffs face stricter venue limits tied to relevant activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect independent inventors and universities with special venue rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill gives the freest rules to independent inventors and to individual inventors and universities, noting their special role in this system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While curbing corporate forum shopping, the reform preserves easier access to courts for small inventors and universities so as not to disadvantage those groups relative to large corporate plaintiffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on patents for tax planning methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision prohibits prospectively the award of patents for tax planning methods and urges reexamination of such patents already issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: tax strategy patents interfere with taxpayers’ ability to comply with the Tax Code without paying royalties; the provision would bar future awards and encourage the PTO to reexamine previously issued tax strategy patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve overall patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Across its range of provisions, the reform measure makes long-needed changes that will improve the quality of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improving patent quality is framed as reducing patent disputes and litigation, helping examiners perform better searches, and ensuring issued patents are reliable tools for innovation and licensing; measures include third-party submissions, post-grant review, and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rein in abusive lawsuits and deter opportunistic litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust aspects of the litigation process to rein in abusive lawsuits and forum shopping so that aggressive trial lawyers do not exploit the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines venue restrictions, damages limits, and willfulness clarifications to reduce the profitability of opportunistic litigation (including entities formed solely to sue) and to protect productive innovators from predatory suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure PTO takes a more careful look before final issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the Patent Office to take a more careful look at the patent and the application that accompanies it before that patent is issued in final form by the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through strengthened post-grant procedures and improved opportunities for input, the PTO is to provide more thorough scrutiny prior to issuing final patents, reducing issuance of weak or invalid patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify inequitable conduct and best mode requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill addresses provisions dealing with inequitable conduct and best mode to help improve patent issuance and patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though details are not exhaustively described on this page, the treatment of inequitable conduct and best mode is presented as part of an effort to reduce litigation uncertainty and focus enforcement on substantive validity and infringement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance protection of inventors with public dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative intent to ensure the patent system continues to reward innovation while encouraging public dissemination and not unduly discouraging innovation through litigation or overly broad patent grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing principle: updates should protect inventors and incentivize R&D while preventing abusive practices that hinder competition or raise costs for consumers; used to justify a suite of reforms rather than single-rule changes.
